definition: Google's former name for its publisher ad-serving platform, subsequently incorporated into Google Ad Manager.
example: A publisher uses the platform to allocate advertising inventory across campaigns.

definition: A specimen collection method in which drops of blood are dried on an absorbent card for later testing.
example: A screening program sends dried specimens to a central laboratory for analysis.

definition: An imaging system that helps vehicle operators see when ordinary visibility is reduced.
example: A vehicle operator uses the display to maintain awareness when visibility is poor.

definition: Operating a vehicle safely and lawfully while adjusting to traffic, road conditions, and its handling characteristics.
example: A driver leaves additional following distance on a wet road.

definition: A United States law addressing oversight of drug compounding and traceability in the prescription drug supply chain.
example: A distributor reviews its product-tracing obligations under the law.

definition: A clinical technique in which a trained practitioner uses fine needles without injecting a substance to address certain musculoskeletal symptoms.
example: A credentialed clinician considers dry needling as one component of a patient's treatment plan.

definition: Installing gypsum wallboard and restoring damaged areas to a sound, finish-ready surface.
example: A contractor patches a damaged wall and finishes its seams.

definition: A suite of enterprise software for property and casualty insurers' policy, billing, and claims operations.
example: An insurer uses a Duck Creek application to administer claims and review their status.

definition: Medical equipment intended for repeated use to support care or daily function.
example: A patient uses a prescribed home wheelchair.
sense_note: Reimbursement programs may apply additional eligibility criteria to this category.

definition: A JavaScript templating library for rendering text or markup from data, including asynchronously supplied data.
example: A website renders a product list after its data service responds.

definition: An inventory auditing approach that adjusts count frequency or priorities as inventory conditions change.
example: A warehouse increases the count frequency for items with recurring discrepancies.

definition: A network protocol that automatically supplies devices with IP addresses and other network configuration settings.
example: A laptop joins an office network and receives a temporary IP address.

definition: A Microsoft business application for scheduling, dispatching, and tracking work performed at customer sites.
example: A dispatcher assigns a repair work order to an available technician.

definition: Promoting goods, services, or organizations through electronic channels and measuring the results.
example: A marketer compares response rates from a newsletter and a paid search campaign.

definition: An iOS user-interface testing framework that synchronizes test interactions with application activity.
example: A test taps a sign-in button and waits for the result before checking the next screen.

definition: A project control system that combines scope, schedule, and cost information to compare completed work with the baseline plan.
example: A project controller compares the budgeted value of completed work with its actual cost.

definition: A protective device that disconnects electrical power when it detects leakage to earth beyond its specified limit.
example: A protective breaker interrupts a circuit after an insulation fault causes leakage.
sense_note: The label can refer to historical voltage-operated devices or modern current-sensing devices.

definition: A JavaScript library for drawing and interacting with graphics on an HTML canvas.
example: A developer uses EaselJS to display interactive sprites in a browser game.

definition: The collection of eBay service interfaces that lets authorized software access marketplace functions and data.
example: A seller's inventory application updates permitted listing details through the interface.

definition: An electronic health record and practice management system used by healthcare providers.
example: A clinic documents an encounter and schedules follow-up in its system.

definition: A population-level study design that relates exposures and outcomes measured for groups rather than individuals.
example: A researcher compares neighborhood-level air quality and asthma rates without inferring individual exposure.

definition: A statistical representation of economic relationships used to estimate effects, test hypotheses, or make forecasts.
example: An analyst uses observed prices and sales to estimate how demand changes with price.

definition: A specification for broadcasting defined data formats from Bluetooth Low Energy beacons.
example: A receiver interprets an Eddystone frame sent by a nearby beacon.
sense_note: Do not assume support for any discontinued Google beacon service.

definition: A nonlinear video editing application for assembling, processing, and exporting footage.
example: An editor combines clips from several cameras into a finished interview.

definition: Specialized instruction and support that addresses barriers to learning and develops adaptive learning strategies.
example: An educational therapist teaches a learner to organize multistep reading tasks.

definition: A structured team method for containing a problem, identifying its root causes, and implementing verified corrective actions.
example: A manufacturer uses an 8D report to investigate and prevent recurring assembly defects.

definition: Salesforce's former branding for an embedded business analytics platform associated with CRM Analytics.
example: A sales manager uses an embedded dashboard to examine changes in pipeline conversion.

definition: A collection of tools for ingesting, searching, analyzing, and visualizing data around Elasticsearch.
example: An operations team searches centralized logs and visualizes service errors over time.

definition: Instruments that measure electrical quantities such as energy use, current, or voltage.
example: A utility uses an energy meter to record electricity consumption for billing.

definition: A vehicle whose propulsion uses one or more electric motors powered by electrical energy.
example: A delivery operator recharges a battery-electric van between shifts.

definition: Identifying faults in electrical equipment or circuits and restoring operation through appropriate repairs.
example: A qualified technician traces a recurring equipment failure to a damaged connection.

definition: Installing and connecting electrical conductors and related components to meet design and safety requirements.
example: A qualified electrician installs wiring for a new lighting circuit according to the approved plan.

definition: An instrument that uses a beam of electrons rather than visible light to produce highly magnified images.
example: A materials scientist uses an electron microscope to examine a fracture surface.

definition: A digital system for collecting, validating, and managing structured data, commonly in clinical studies.
example: A research coordinator enters scheduled visit observations into an electronic case report form.

definition: Creating and transmitting prescriptions electronically through an authorized clinical system.
example: A clinician sends an approved prescription directly to the patient's chosen pharmacy.

definition: Preparing and distributing written or multimedia publications in digital formats.
example: A publisher exports an accessible electronic edition for distribution through a digital storefront.

definition: A medical technique that uses high-frequency electrical current to cut tissue or control bleeding.
example: A trained surgeon uses an electrosurgical instrument during an operation.

definition: Applying professional norms of clarity, tone, privacy, and responsiveness in electronic correspondence.
example: An employee uses a descriptive subject and moves sensitive details to an approved private channel.

definition: An email quality assurance tool for previewing messages and checking compatibility across email clients.
example: A designer previews a campaign in several inbox layouts to catch rendering errors.

definition: Services that send, receive, host, or manage electronic email for users or organizations.
example: A marketing team selects a provider to send newsletters and track delivery.
sense_note: May refer to mailbox hosting or bulk and transactional delivery platforms depending on context.
